title: Make loading, errors, and controls understandable
outcome: Design accessible states and measure a real user-visible delay.
cue: Show progress. Keep work. Offer recovery.

trace.title: User intent
trace.detail:
# The idea

A useful screen explains what is happening and what the user can do next. Design initial, loading, empty, ready, saving, failed, and retry states.

Keep an unsaved draft when a save fails. An empty list and a failed request should not look identical.

Use real buttons for actions and links for navigation. Labels must identify form controls.

Keyboard users need a visible focus indicator and a sensible focus order. Errors should name the field and explain a repair.

Color alone is not enough.

Performance starts with measurement. LCP concerns major content appearing, INP concerns responsiveness, and CLS concerns unexpected layout movement.

A fast API does not guarantee a responsive page if JavaScript blocks the main thread. Measure on representative devices and data.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Trace user intent → action → immediate feedback → result → recovery. During saving, prevent accidental duplicate actions while explaining progress.

On failure, keep the input and offer retry. If a modal closes, restore focus to the control that opened it.

Use a performance profile to find the long task behind an unresponsive click. Split work, reduce unnecessary rendering, or virtualize a genuinely large list after measuring.

Do not add memoization to every line without evidence.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail:
A spinner without context can feel stuck. A disabled control may hide why an action is unavailable.

A click-only div is not equivalent to a keyboard-accessible button.
